doc: metrics.measure on a map: global_mean, zonal profile (5-degree bands: centers and means), area-weighted 10-bin histogram, the 56 gnomonic patches (patches) each measured by coherence, spectral_slope and object_stats, then coherence and spectral_slope = mean over patches (np.nanmean for the slope: NaN patches are skipped), coherence_by_lat = mean over the 8 longitudes of each of the 7 latitudes (PATCH_LATS order), big_object_share = mean of the per-patch shares, median_object_km2 = np.median over the 56 per-patch medians (even count: mean of the middle two), seam_ratio, pole_std. Extra outputs patch_coherence, patch_slope, patch_big, patch_median are the 56 per-patch values (patches order: latitude-major) recomputed by the case through the same calls, to localize a difference. The 256x128 Earth reference (smooth: its patches are ~18x upsampled, coherence ~0.84, slope ~-5.1). Tolerances, measured by moving every texel of the map by -1, 0 or +1 float32 ulp at random (6 trials on each of four maps, Earth at 256 and 512, an isotropic and a stirred generated map) and by promoting the map to float64, each set to about 10x the largest change seen: global_mean 5e-9, zonal 1.2e-7 and seam_ratio 2.4e-7 and pole_std 8e-8 (float32 row statistics: the float32 default); aggregated coherence 1.5e-9 and coherence_by_lat 5.3e-9 (1e-7 relative), spectral_slope 1.2e-8 (3e-8 relative), per-patch coherence 2.7e-8 (5e-7) and per-patch slope 3.2e-7 (1e-6): the sensitivity of a float64 chain to float32 rounding of the map, which a port that samples its patches in float64 never sees; hist and the bin ties: see area_histogram (1e-9 holds for a port that sends a texel equal to a float32 edge to the upper bin, which u8 / 255 maps do for 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8); the per-patch big share and median are hard thresholds (a texel crossing 0.5 can move a whole object across 1e5 km^2; no flip occurred in 24 nudged runs, the largest change was 3.8e-6) and carry a `frac` of 0.05 (2 of 56 patches may differ), the aggregated values the default floor.  Input convention: the u8 input(s) img are maps stored as bytes, and the function receives them as float32(u8) / float32(255) (`u8.astype(np.float32) / 255.0`: the division is done, and correctly rounded, in float32, as measure.load reads an 8-bit map), NOT as the raw bytes and NOT as a float64 quotient (a texel on a histogram edge or a threshold would move). params.u8_inputs lists them.

params.input: u8 / 255 as float32 (the 8-bit map measure.py loads)

u8_inputs.img: float32(u8) / float32(255), the division in float32
